implementation_notes: TypeScript can make the envy measurable rather than merely visible: declare the operation as a function whose only parameter is the data interface, and any reader sees that nothing else is used. Moving it is then a matter of putting it on the interface's implementation (or as a free function with the interface as its parameter type, which keeps the interface narrow). The `unknown`-over-`any` rule matters here: with `any` on the data shape the envy is unreviewable.
idiom_name: function typed on the wrong interface
pitfalls: Structural typing means the envy can be satisfied by any matching shape, so moving a method onto an interface can break callers subtly when the shape widens.
A generic constraint `<T extends HasName>` is a way of making the envy explicit, but it does not move the knowledge.
`readonly` on the fields makes the type look safe while the envious function still recomputes the same derived value.
